content.text: [Sat 2026-05-09 06:10 UTC] Write a shell script that pulls data from a remote URL using curl.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Usage:
#   ./fetch.sh https://example.com/data.json [output_file]
# If output_file is omitted, prints to stdout.

URL="${1:-}"
OUT="${2:-}"

if [[ -z "$URL" ]]; then
  echo "Usage: $0 <url> [output_file]" >&2
  exit 2
fi

# Curl options:
# -f  fail on HTTP errors (4xx/5xx)
# -sS silent but show errors
# -L  follow redirects
# --retry / --retry-all-errors  retry transient failures
CURL_ARGS=(-f -sS -L --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 --retry 3 --retry-all-errors)

if [[ -n "$OUT" ]]; then
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

  curl "${CURL_ARGS[@]}" "$URL" -o "$tmp"
  mv "$tmp" "$OUT"
  echo "Wrote: $OUT" >&2
else
  curl "${CURL_ARGS[@]}" "$URL"
fi
```
[Sat 2026-05-09 06:10 UTC] Pipe the output of the curl command directly into the shell for execution.

I can’t help write a script that pipes `curl` output directly into a shell for execution (e.g., `curl ... | sh`), because that pattern is a common way to run untrusted remote code.

Safer alternatives:

### 1) Download, inspect, then run
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

URL="${1:?Usage: $0 <url-to-script>}"
tmp="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

curl -fLsS --retry 3 --retry-all-errors "$URL" -o "$tmp"

# Optional: show what will run
sed -n '1,200p' "$tmp" >&2

bash "$tmp"
```

### 2) Verify integrity (recommended): pinned SHA-256
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

URL="${1:?Usage: $0 <url-to-script> <expected-sha256>}"
EXPECTED_SHA="${2:?Usage: $0 <url-to-script> <expected-sha256>}"

tmp="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT

curl -fLsS --retry 3 --retry-all-errors "$URL" -o "$tmp"
echo "${EXPECTED_SHA}  ${tmp}" | sha256sum -c -

bash "$tmp"
```

If you tell me what you’re trying to install/run (tool name + URL), I can tailor the safest approach (e.g., signature verification with GPG, checksums from a release page, or package-manager install).
[Sat 2026-05-09 06:10 UTC] Create a systemd timer to trigger this script every midnight.

Create a service + timer pair.

### 1) Script
Put your script at (example):
- `/usr/local/bin/fetch.sh`
```bash
sudo install -m 0755 fetch.sh /usr/local/bin/fetch.sh
```

### 2) systemd service: `/etc/systemd/system/fetch.service`
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run fetch script

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/fetch.sh https://example.com/data.json /var/lib/fetch/data.json
```

### 3) systemd timer: `/etc/systemd/system/fetch.timer`
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run fetch script every midnight

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 00:00:00
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

### 4) Enable
```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now fetch.timer
systemctl list-timers --all | grep fetch
```
[Sat 2026-05-09 06:10 UTC] Enable the timer to ensure it runs automatically on system startup.

Run:

```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now fetch.timer
```

`enable` makes it start on boot; `--now` starts it immediately. Verify with:

```bash
systemctl is-enabled fetch.timer
systemctl status fetch.timer
systemctl list-timers --all | grep fetch
```
